answer: Bindings are kept in opal, verified in copper, and the chain is public. Each challenge is bound to the identity's previous 6 answers, so the new answer must be consistent with them or be rejected at the haven check. A farm generating text without memory of its own history therefore fails the binding, which means it has to store and read state per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 212 aliases cost 164 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
